title: TAP DANCE BASICS - 5 Steps EVERY Beginner should Master

observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

extraction.teacher_style: The teacher uses a clear, encouraging tone and breaks down steps into simple, manageable components. He emphasizes proper technique and provides helpful tips to avoid common mistakes.

lesson_structure.note: The teacher introduces the topic of basic tap dance steps.
The teacher explains and demonstrates the ball-heel step.
The teacher explains and demonstrates the brush step.
The teacher explains and demonstrates the shuffle step.
The teacher explains and demonstrates the ball-change step.
The teacher explains and demonstrates the flap step.
The teacher explains and demonstrates the flap-heel step.
The teacher explains and demonstrates the stomp and stamp steps.
The teacher leads a practice session of the learned steps with music.

metaphors: bread and butter of the form
common_mistakes: swinging the leg back too far
shuffling and then stepping instead of doing a flap
safety: don't pound too much on a hard surface to avoid shin splints

steps_taught.name: Ball-Heel
steps_taught.description: Lift the foot, place the ball of the foot down, then drop the heel.

steps_taught.name: Brush
steps_taught.description: Brush the ball of the foot forward and then back.

steps_taught.name: Shuffle
steps_taught.description: A forward brush followed by a backward brush.

steps_taught.name: Ball-Change
steps_taught.description: Step on the ball of the foot, then shift weight to the other foot.

steps_taught.name: Flap
steps_taught.description: A brush forward followed by a step on the whole foot.

steps_taught.name: Flap-Heel
steps_taught.description: A flap followed by a heel drop.

steps_taught.name: Stomp
steps_taught.description: Hit the floor with the whole foot and lift it back up.

steps_taught.name: Stamp
steps_taught.description: Hit the floor with the whole foot and keep the weight on it.

quotes.text: They are the bread and butter of the form.
It's just a long for the ride, as I like to say.
It sounds like fa-lap because we're just following the syllables of our footwork.
You don't want to pound too much, because you will give yourself shin splints.

evidence_segments.observation: The teacher demonstrates the ball-heel step, showing the foot lift, ball placement, and heel drop.
The teacher demonstrates how to shake out ankles to release tension.
The teacher demonstrates the shuffle step, showing the forward and backward brush.
The teacher demonstrates the flap step, showing the brush forward and the step.

extraction.distinctive_method: The teacher uses the syllables of the step names to help students remember the rhythm and timing of the movements.
